data.title: Staples Canada launches Staples Business to unify B2B offerings
data.description:
Staples Canada has launched Staples Business, a new brand in the market to bring office supplies, technology, print and facilities services together for Canadian business customers.

The brand will focus on two tiers: one for smaller businesses and one for larger buyers that need custom pricing and dedicated account support.

Richmond Hill, Ontario-based Staples Canada said the new brand would simplify purchasing and account management for business customers.

Why Staples Business is launching in Canada

“Staples Business brings everything our business customers rely on together under one brand, building on our long-standing commitment to supporting Canadian businesses for more than 30 years,” said Chris Saniga, chief B2B officer at Staples Canada. “As a Canadian company, we understand the pressures organizations here are facing. Whether it’s a growing startup or a large enterprise, our goal is to take more off their plate so they can focus on what comes next.”

Currently, Staples has nearly 300 outlets in Canada. Its Quebec stores operate under the Bureau en Gros nameplate.

Industry analysts assessed that the new brand’s debut is as much about competition as customer service.

Marty Bauer, ecommerce expert at Omnisend, an email and SMS marketing platform for ecommerce brands, said the move was necessary to fend off competition.

“This new branding strategy is about much more than a cosmetic rebrand,” Bauer stated. “It’s an important step in defending the market against ecommerce giants, particularly Amazon Business.”

What makes Staples Canada’s business customer unique?

Bauer noted that B2B clients are quite different from regular shoppers in Staples Canada’s case.

“The goal is to make supply procurement as easy and frictionless as possible,” he said. “It’s as much about time and efficiency as it is about price. The new, refreshed Staples Business aims to offer exactly that.”

Bauer added that Staples Business has brought together a wide range of products, from office and janitorial supplies to IT hardware.

“This means a single account manager is responsible for all of a client’s needs, which significantly lowers administrative hassle for both parties,” Bauer said.

Additionally, Bauer pointed out that Staples Business will be able to categorize its clients into different tiers. Different-sized businesses require different approaches. For instance, small-to-medium businesses (SMBs) may place greater emphasis on an automated checkout system, transparency and fast response times than larger companies. Meanwhile, large businesses, Bauer explained, expect dynamic contract pricing, custom product catalogs and dedicated account managers.

“Staples Business is now better able to cater to these different needs,” Bauer said.

How Staples Business will try to compete in Canada

Lastly, Bauer said, a dedicated B2B brand could show Staples Canada’s business customers that a company is serious about catering to them and can compete with ecommerce giants.

“They may not be able to compete in terms of pricing, but they can compete in terms of expertise and the ability to cater to clients’ specific needs,” Bauer said.

Another observer said the brand’s success will depend on whether Staples can deliver on its promise.

Rich Pleeth, founder of the artificial intelligence (AI)-powered logistics platform Finmile, said a dedicated business brand can help Staples Canada win customers by making its wider offer easier to understand.

“Someone who thinks of Staples for printer paper may not think of it for IT support or facilities supplies,” Pleeth stated. “Putting those services together gives the sales team a clearer story, but the customer still needs a reason to change suppliers.”

Pleeth echoed Bauer’s perspective, adding that a small business might be persuaded by the prospect of less time spent ordering and chasing deliveries.

“For a larger buyer, consolidated invoicing, agreed pricing and an account manager who can sort out a problem could be worth more than a small discount on stationery,” Pleeth said. “The two tiers make sense because those buyers need different levels of support.”

Nevertheless, Pleeth expects that the new name will present a test.

“If a business orders laptops, chairs and printed materials for a new office, can someone coordinate the delivery and resolve anything missing?” he asked. “If the customer still has to chase three departments, the brand has promised more than the operation delivers.”

data.title: David's Bridal plans to spin off its AI-powered Pearl platform
data.description:
In 2025, David’s Bridal’s Shopify transition paved the way for an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) reimagining of its Pearl wedding planner — and now, the company has plans to spin off Pearl as its own entity.

K&F Growth Acquisition Corp. II, as special purposed acquisition company, announced alongside David’s Bridal, that the two companies had signed a nonbinding letter of intent to carry out a process to that would see Pearl go public.

Ultimately, their plan also calls for Pearl to eventually own David’s Bridal’s brand and intellectual property.

David’s Bridal is No. 460 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

David’s Bridal is also No. 178 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

data.title: 1-800-Flowers.com sells two business units to PlanetArt
data.description:
Less than one month after a final deal was announced, 1-800-Flowers.com confirmed that the sale of its PersonalizationMall.com and Things Remembered units to PlanetArt is now complete.

1-800-Flowers.com’s sale to the technology platform marks a step forward during a challenging year for the flowers and gifts retailer as it seeks to focus its business priorities and address falling revenue.

1-800-Flowers.com is No. 67 in the Top 1000 Database. The database tracks North America’s leading online retailers based on their annual ecommerce sales and more.

1-800-Flowers.com is also No. 76 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

1-800-Flowers.com web sales by year

Why 1-800-Flowers.com sold PersonalizationMall.com and Things Remembered to PlanetArt

“The sale of PersonalizationMall.com enables us to further sharpen our portfolio focus, strengthen our financial position and create additional capacity to invest in the strategic initiatives we believe offer the greatest opportunity to drive improved performance and long-term growth,” said Adolfo Villagomez, CEO at 1-800-Flowers.com, in a released statement on Sept. 29. “As we continue to simplify our business, we are taking a disciplined approach to where ownership creates strategic value and where partnerships can provide a more efficient way to serve our customers.”

Villagomez framed the move as part of a wider effort to correct course at the company.

“This transaction reflects that approach and provides us with greater financial flexibility as we continue executing our transformation and positioning the Company for sustainable, profitable growth,” he stated. “We believe PlanetArt is a strong strategic fit for PersonalizationMall.com and Things Remembered and is well positioned to support the business’s continued growth and success.”

Following the sale, 1-800-Flowers.com expected to reach a deal with PlanetArt that would result in 1-800-Flowers.com continuing to offer some PersonalizationMall.com products.

Are 1-800-Flowers.com’s digital sales growing?

“Throughout fiscal 2026, we strengthened our leadership team, simplified our organization, began to modernize our digital and marketing capabilities, improved operational efficiency, and increasingly put the customer at the center of everything we do,” Villagomez told investors during a Sept. 10 earnings call.

Total ecommerce sales for 1-800-Flowers.com fell by 13.1% year over year to $1.27 billion in results from its fiscal 2026 ended June 28. Over the same period, total revenue declined 10.8% to $1.50 billion.

Villagomez arrived at 1-800-Flowers.com as CEO in 2025, with his background leading online efforts at Home Depot as a prominent part of his résumé. Since then, he has focused on modernization and efficiencies to execute a turnaround.

“As we enter fiscal 2027, accelerating the recovery of our revenue trends is our highest priority,” he said in September. “We will continue building these capabilities while increasingly putting them to work to improve customer acquisition, engagement, and retention and to drive better business performance over time.”

data.title: Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus memberships to come bundled in $120 subscription
data.description:
Walmart Inc. will bundle memberships for its Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus programs, making a bet that shoppers will subscribe to both when given the chance to save nearly $100.

The paid membership programs for Walmart and its sibling chain of club locations both include free delivery options, as well as lineups of other perks that will be offered together for a $120 annual fee.

Walmart ranks No. 2 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

In addition, Walmart is No. 37 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus memberships are being offered together

“We’re giving people a reason to expect more from their memberships,” said John Furner, president and CEO at Walmart. “For $120 a year, we’re raising expectations for what a membership can deliver: more money in their pockets and more time to call their own.”

In a list of features and benefits published by Walmart, the company outlined 26 perks that it would make available, including those from the standalone Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus plans, as well as four that do not appear outside of the combined bundle. Those include:

  • Pharmacy savings
  • Savings on optical and hearing
  • Early shopping
  • An annual $60 electronic gift card for T-Mobile

For existing Walmart+ members under the retailer’s annual plan, the combined membership means an additional $22 annual cost. Meanwhile, the company said the Sam’s Club Plus members could add Walmart+ to their existing subscription at no extra cost. Sam’s Club members who do not already pay for Plus will be charged $60 more per year to add both memberships to their accounts.

Benefits from the individual Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus memberships

Both Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus have added new incentives in recent years, expanding their work with partners to build out benefits to compete with other paid membership programs such as Amazon Prime and Target Circle 360.

In the latest announcement, Walmart highlighted streaming access to either Peacock or Paramount+, as well as savings of 10 cents a gallon at more than 17,000 participating stations, among the combined subscription’s selling points.

Sam’s Club added Weight Watchers options to its program over the summer. In 2024, Walmart incorporated Burger King purchase savings into its memberships.

data.title: Wildfire and Badge bring merchant rewards into Apple, Google and Samsung wallets
data.description:
The loyalty platform Wildfire Systems and mobile wallet infrastructure provider Badge are partnering to push merchant offers and cashback rewards to more shoppers through popular payment methods. The companies announced their partnership at the Money20/20 USA event in Las Vegas.

Together, Wildfire and Badge will allow merchants to extend existing rewards programs to additional payment tools that a customer may already be using. The options will reach both online purchases and purchases in physical stores.

The new deal connects Wildfire’s network of more than 50,000 merchants to Badge’s digital wallet infrastructure, which includes Apple Wallet, Google Wallet and Samsung Wallet. 

How the Wildfire-Badge partnership will work

When a consumer adds a rewards pass to their mobile wallet, it will then surface personalized cashback and savings offers from merchants in Wildfire’s network. As offers change or new deals become relevant, the pass updates automatically. 

Consumers also receive push notifications when new offers are available. The pass can surface location-aware reminders when a shopper is near a participating merchant’s physical store. When the shopper is ready to buy, either online or in store, the offer is prepared and presented to them in their wallet.

Attribution and tracking are handled by Wildfire’s platform on the back end, so neither the merchant nor the loyalty program operator needs to build separate infrastructure to support wallet-based offers.

“Our partnership with Badge gives clients a way to extend their existing rewards programs into mobile wallets, meeting their customers where they are to discover and use offers,” Wildfire CEO Jordan Glazier said in a written statement. “In turn, our merchant network gives Badge’s clients a steady stream of relevant offers to put in front of their customers.”

The system is designed to work across both digital and physical retail. For online purchases, the offer appears in the wallet app and is applied at checkout. For an in-store purchase, the same wallet a consumer taps to pay also carries the relevant cashback offer, connecting the payment moment to the rewards program.

What Wildfire and Badge do with retailers

Wildfire is a commerce intelligence platform that provides retail media and rewards program services for financial services and technology companies. Visa, Citi and RBC are among its clients. Wildfire’s merchants include high-profile retailers such as Best Buy, Macy’s and Ulta Beauty.

Best Buy ranks No. 8 in the Top 1000 Database. The Top 1000 is Digital Commerce 360’s market research tool that tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales. There, Ulta Beauty ranks No. 37, and Macy’s ranks No. 18.

Meanwhile, Badge is a platform that allows clients to make mobile wallets programmable to drive engagement and sales. 

“The next evolution of mobile wallets is about what happens beyond the transaction,” Badge CEO Eric Senn said. “By combining our technology with Wildfire’s merchant offer network, we can help our clients put relevant savings opportunities directly into consumers’ hands, whether they’re shopping online or walking into a store.”
